words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.ex: His excuse was laughable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口可笑极了。
words.en: If you describe something as laughable, you mean that it is so silly or unreasonable that you can only laugh at it.

words.ex: He wore a laurel crown on his head.
words.ex_cn: 他头上戴着月桂花环。
words.en: A laurel is a type of shrub or tree, specifically the bay tree, whose leaves are used in cooking and as a symbol of victory or honor.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 无法律的；不遵守法律的；目无法纪的
words.ex: The town was plagued by lawless gangs.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇被无法无天的帮派所困扰。
words.en: If you describe a country or a situation as lawless, you mean that laws do not exist or are not obeyed, and people are not protected from crime.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: The movie was banned for its lewd content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因内容猥亵而被禁播。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as lewd, you are critical of it because it is sexual in a rude and unpleasant way.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；自由主义的；
n. 自由党党员；
words.ex: He is a liberal teacher who listens to students.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，会倾听学生的声音。
words.en: A liberal person, system, or policy is one that is in favour of allowing people a lot of freedom in their behaviour or opinions.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.tr:
n. 登徒子；浪荡子；好色之徒
adj. 放荡的；自由思想的
words.ex: He lived a libertine life, ignoring all rules.
words.ex_cn: 他过着放荡的生活，无视所有规则。
words.en: A libertine is someone who behaves without moral principles or a sense of responsibility, especially in sexual matters.

words.ex: He got a driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A license is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.

words.ex: He gave a licentious speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上发表了一篇放荡不羁的演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person as licentious, you mean that they are very immoral in their sexual behavior.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He loves reading literary books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读文学书籍。
words.en: Literary means concerned with or connected with the writing, study, or appreciation of literature.

words.ex: He is literate and can read simple books.
words.ex_cn: 他有读写能力，能读简单的书。
words.en: A literate person is able to read and write, and has a good education.

words.tr: adj. 易弯的；柔软的；动作轻盈的
words.ex: The dancer is lithe and moves gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者身材柔韧，动作优雅。
words.en: A person or animal that is lithe is thin, supple, and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 不乐意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He is loath to apologize for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: If you are loath to do something, you do not want to do it.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的；可恶的；令人憎恶的
words.ex: The smell of the rotten food was loathsome.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人作呕。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as loathsome, you are indicating that they are extremely unpleasant and disgusting.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.ex: He used a common locution in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个常见的表达方式。
words.en: A particular style or manner of speaking; a phrase or expression.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: He was regarded as a clumsy lout by his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的同事们认为他是个笨拙的人。
words.en: A lout is a man who behaves in a rude and aggressive way.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；可怜的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: Her lugubrious expression made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 她那悲哀的表情让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is lugubrious, you mean that they are sad and solemn.

words.ex: There was a lull in the rain before the storm came back.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨再次来临前，雨下了一阵间歇。
words.en: A lull is a short period of quiet or calm in an otherwise noisy or hectic situation. To lull means to cause someone to feel calm or to fall asleep.

words.ex: The mother sang a lullaby to her baby.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈为她的宝宝唱了一首摇篮曲。
words.en: A lullaby is a quiet song which is intended to be sung to babies and young children to help them go to sleep.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.tr:
n. 强烈的性欲；强烈的欲望
v. 对…有极强的性欲（或欲望）
words.ex: His lust for power ruined his relationships.
words.ex_cn: 他对权力的强烈欲望毁掉了他的关系。
words.en: Lust is a strong feeling of wanting to have or to do something, especially sexual desire.

words.ex: The lustrous pearl shone under the light.
words.ex_cn: 这颗有光泽的珍珠在光下闪耀。
words.en: Something that is lustrous shines brightly and gently, often because it is very smooth or clean.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；生气勃勃的；健壮的
words.ex: The young man sang a lusty song at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个年轻人在派对上唱了一首嘹亮的歌。
words.en: If you describe someone as lusty, you mean that they are strong and healthy and full of energy.

words.tr: n. 奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；
words.ex: She bought a luxury dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件奢华的裙子。
words.en: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

words.tr:
n. 抒情诗；歌词
adj. 抒情的
words.ex: He wrote a lyric about the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于日落的抒情诗。
words.en: Lyric refers to the words of a song, especially a popular song, or to a short poem that expresses personal feelings and thoughts.

words.ex: The machinations of the rival company were uncovered.
words.ex_cn: 竞争对手公司的阴谋被揭露了。
words.en: A machination is a plot or scheme, especially one that is complex or devious.

words.ex: He showed magnanimity by forgiving his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽恕了敌人，展现了宽宏大量。
words.en: Magnanimity is the quality of being kind, generous, and forgiving, especially towards someone who has wronged you.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 夸张的话；豪语；大言
words.ex: The politician's speech was filled with magniloquence, but lacked concrete plans.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家的演讲充满了豪言壮语，但缺乏具体的计划。
words.en: Magniloquence is the use of high-flown language; bombast.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不服的
n. 不满现状的人；反抗者
words.ex: The malcontent workers complained about low pay.
words.ex_cn: 不满的员工抱怨工资太低。
words.en: A malcontent is a person who is dissatisfied and rebellious.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: The malevolent wizard cast a dark spell.
words.ex_cn: 那个有恶意的巫师施了一个黑暗咒语。
words.en: Having or showing a wish to harm others; malicious.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: He was accused of malingering to avoid military service.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控装病以逃避兵役。
words.en: If someone is malingering, they pretend to be ill in order to avoid work or duties.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: The child has malnutrition from not eating enough food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子因为吃不够饭而营养不良。
words.en: Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess (too high in intake), or in the wrong proportions.

words.tr: adj. 恶臭的；有恶臭的；有臭味的
words.ex: The malodorous garbage was attracting flies.
words.ex_cn: 那堆有恶臭的垃圾招来了苍蝇。
words.en: Having a very unpleasant smell.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: She put the wet clothes into the mangle to remove the water.
words.ex_cn: 她把湿衣服放进衣物轧干机里去除水分。
words.en: To mangle something means to severely damage it, usually by twisting, tearing, or cutting it, so that it is no longer in its original condition.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: He spoke in a polite manner.
words.ex_cn: 他以礼貌的方式说话。
words.en: The way in which something is done or happens.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.tr: v. （使）留痕迹；做标记；评分；“mark”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 明显的；显著的；有记号的；
words.ex: The storm marked the old tree with deep scratches.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在那棵老树上留下了深深的划痕。
words.en: A marked change or difference is very obvious and easily noticed.

words.tr: n. 要求严格纪律的人；严格执行纪律者
words.ex: The sergeant was a martinet who insisted on absolute obedience from his troops.
words.ex_cn: 这位中士是一个严格执行纪律的人，他坚持要求他的部队绝对服从。
words.en: A martinet is someone who demands strict adherence to rules and discipline.

words.ex: He has a masculine voice and strong build.
words.ex_cn: 他声音低沉，身材强壮。
words.en: Having qualities or appearance traditionally associated with men.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr: adj. 善于掌控局势的；精彩的；精湛的
words.ex: He gave a masterful speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上发表了一篇精湛的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as masterful, you mean that they behave in a way which shows that they are in control of a situation and can command respect from other people.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece by art critics.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被艺术评论家视为杰作。
words.en: A masterpiece is a work of art such as a painting, film, or book that is made with great skill and is considered to be the best work of a particular artist or writer.

words.tr:
n. 材料；原料；
adj. 物质的；
words.ex: The table is made of wood material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由木头材料制成的。
words.en: Material refers to the substance or substances from which a thing is made or can be made, or information or ideas for use in creating a book or other work.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodious song at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时唱出旋律优美的歌。
words.en: If something such as a voice or a tune is melodious, it is pleasant to listen to because it has a musical quality.

words.ex: The cell has a thin membrane.
words.ex_cn: 细胞有一层薄薄的膜。
words.en: A membrane is a thin layer of tissue or material that covers or lines a part of the body, or separates one area from another.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.tr: adj. 值得纪念的；难忘的；
words.ex: That vacation was a memorable trip.
words.ex_cn: 那次旅行是一次值得纪念的旅程。
words.en: Something that is memorable is worth remembering or likely to be remembered, because it is special or very enjoyable.

words.ex: They built a statue to memorialize the hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们建了一座雕像来纪念这位英雄。
words.en: To memorialize something means to do something that makes people remember it, especially by creating a statue or monument.

words.ex: He tries to memorize the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天试着记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorize something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈悲的；宽大的
words.ex: The judge was merciful and gave him a small fine.
words.ex_cn: 法官很仁慈，只判了他一笔小额罚款。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as merciful, you mean that they show or have mercy.

words.tr: adj. 残忍的；无情的；无慈悲心的；
words.ex: The merciless storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场残忍的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe someone as merciless, you mean that they are very cruel or determined and do not show any concern for the effect their actions have on other people.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 值得嘉奖的；有功的
words.ex: Her work on the project was meritorious and earned her a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 她在项目中的工作是有功的，为她赢得了晋升。
words.en: Deserving reward or praise; having merit.

words.ex: The children laughed with merriment at the circus.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在马戏团里开心地大笑。
words.en: Merriment is the quality or state of being merry, characterized by joy and laughter.

words.tr: v. 施以催眠术；迷住；迷惑
words.ex: The dancer mesmerized the crowd with her slow movements.
words.ex_cn: 舞者用她缓慢的动作对观众施以催眠术。
words.en: If you are mesmerized by something, you are so interested in it or so attracted to it that you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: His metabolic rate is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢率很高。
words.en: Relating to or involving the chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.tr:
v. （使）生气
n. 发脾气；微怒
words.ex: She got a miff when I forgot her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记了她的生日，她有点恼火。
words.en: To cause to be annoyed or offended.

words.ex: The migrant found a new job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移居者在城市里找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, especially in order to find work.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.tr:
adj. 一千年的
n. 千禧世代
words.ex: Millennial workers prefer flexible hours.
words.ex_cn: 千禧一代的员工更喜欢灵活的工作时间。
words.en: Relating to a millennium or the millennials, the generation of people born between the early 1980s and the late 1990s.

words.ex: He performed a mime on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上表演了哑剧。
words.en: A mime is a form of performance art where the performer uses gestures and movements without speech to convey a story or emotion. As a verb, to mime means to imitate or mimic actions or expressions without using words.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: The minuscule dot was hard to see with the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 那个极小的点用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr:
n. 分钟；一会儿；
adj. 微小的；极小的；
words.ex: I waited for five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我等了五分钟。
words.en: A minute is a unit of time equal to sixty seconds or a sixtieth of an hour.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.ex: He did misappropriate the company's money.
words.ex_cn: 他确实挪用了公司的钱。
words.en: If someone misappropriates money or property that does not belong to them, they take it without permission and use it for their own purposes.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；淘气；伤害；损害
words.ex: The boy caused mischief by letting the cats out.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩放出了猫，惹了麻烦。
words.en: Mischief is behavior, especially by children, that is slightly bad but is not intended to cause serious harm or damage.

words.tr: n. 轻罪；品行不端；轻刑罪
words.ex: He committed a misdemeanor by parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他因非法停车而犯下轻罪。
words.en: A misdemeanor is a less serious crime than a felony, punishable by less than a year of imprisonment.

words.tr: v. 指错方向；误导；使用不当
words.ex: The instructions were misdirected and led us to the wrong location.
words.ex_cn: 这些指示误导了我们，导致我们去了错误的地方。
words.en: To direct someone or something incorrectly or towards the wrong place or purpose.

words.ex: The miser saved all his money and never spent it.
words.ex_cn: 这个吝啬鬼把所有的钱都存起来，从不花掉。
words.en: A miser is a person who is extremely unwilling to spend money, often to the point of living in poverty despite having wealth.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.tr: adj. 错误的； v. “misguide”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His misguided decision cost him his job.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的决定让他丢了工作。
words.en: If you describe an opinion or plan as misguided, you are critical of it because you think it is based on an incorrect idea or judgment.

words.ex: He misinterprets her words as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的话，以为是生气。
words.en: To interpret wrongly; misunderstand.

words.ex: He misleads his friends with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚假的故事误导他的朋友。
words.en: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

words.tr: n. 误称…之名；不当之名
words.ex: Calling a tomato a vegetable is a misnomer.
words.ex_cn: 把番茄称为蔬菜是一种错误的称呼。
words.en: A misnomer is a name that is wrongly or unsuitably applied to someone or something.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 失去的；失踪的； v. 错失；“miss”的现在分词；
words.ex: The missing book was found under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 那本丢失的书在床下找到了。
words.en: If someone or something is missing, they are not in their usual place, and you cannot find them.

words.ex: The missionary taught children in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 这位传教士在一个小村庄里教孩子们。
words.en: A missionary is a person who is sent to a foreign country to spread a religion.

words.ex: He received a missive from the headquarters.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了来自总部的公函。
words.en: A missive is a letter or other written message.

words.tr: n. 误解；误会； v. “misunderstand”的现在分词；
words.ex: There was a misunderstanding between them about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间对时间产生了误解。
words.en: A misunderstanding is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to confusion or disagreement.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The soil has too much moisture.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中有太多湿气。
words.en: Moisture is tiny drops of water in the air, on a surface, or in a substance, that make it feel wet.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.tr:
v. 脱毛；换毛
n. 脱毛；换毛
words.ex: The bird molts its feathers every spring.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每年春天都会脱毛。
words.en: When an animal molts, it loses its feathers, hair, or skin so that new ones can grow.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；瞬间的；刹那间的
words.ex: The light made a momentary flash.
words.ex_cn: 灯光闪了一下，但只持续了一瞬间。
words.en: lasting for a very short time

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: The monetary policy affects prices.
words.ex_cn: 货币政策影响价格。
words.en: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；不朽作品；
words.ex: The ancient monument attracts many tourists each year.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代历史遗迹每年吸引许多游客。
words.en: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an important person or event.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: The car got stuck in a morass after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨过后，汽车陷在了沼泽地里。
words.en: A morass is a complicated or confused situation that is difficult to get out of, or a stretch of low, soft, wet ground; a marsh.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.tr: n. 荒野；[地理]沼泽；系泊（moor 的复数）; v. 使停泊；被系住（moor 的三单形式）
words.ex: The sheep walk on the moors near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在村庄附近的荒原上行走。
words.en: Moors are areas of open, uncultivated land, often covered with heather, that are found in parts of Britain and other countries.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.tr:
n. 凡人
adj. 致命的；终有一死的
words.ex: All mortal beings must die someday.
words.ex_cn: 所有凡人都终有一死。
words.en: If you refer to the fact that people are mortal, you mean that they have to die and cannot live forever.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.ex: A mote of dust floated in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 一粒微尘在阳光中飘浮。
words.en: A very small piece of a substance, especially dust.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.tr:
v. 使有杂色；使斑驳
n. 斑点；杂色；斑驳
words.ex: The leaves mottle with brown spots in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 秋天时，树叶上出现了褐色斑点。
words.en: To mark with spots or blotches of different shades or colors.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.ex: The cloud has a multiform shape.
words.ex_cn: 云朵有着多变的形状。
words.en: Having or occurring in many forms or shapes.

words.tr: n. 大数目；多种多样；繁多
words.ex: There is a multiplicity of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有大量星星。
words.en: A multiplicity of things or people means a large number or great variety of them.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: A multitude of people attended the festival.
words.ex_cn: 大量的人参加了这个节日。
words.en: A multitude of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: The old book had a musty smell.
words.ex_cn: 那本旧书有一股霉味。
words.en: A musty smell is unpleasant and stale, often because something is old and has not been used or aired for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 可变的；易变的；性情不定的
words.ex: Her mood is as mutable as the weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的情绪就像天气一样多变。
words.en: Capable of or subject to change or alteration.

words.ex: The scientist studied a mutant frog with three legs.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了一只有三条腿的突变青蛙。
words.en: A mutant is an organism or a new genetic character arising or resulting from an instance of mutation.

words.ex: He has myopia and needs glasses to see far objects.
words.ex_cn: 他有近视，需要戴眼镜才能看清远处的物体。
words.en: Myopia is a condition of the eye where light focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina. This results in distant objects appearing blurry while close objects can be seen clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: The stock price hit its nadir last month.
words.ex_cn: 股票价格上个月跌至最低点。
words.en: The nadir of something is the worst or lowest point that it reaches.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.tr: v. 叙述；给（电视或电影）作旁白
words.ex: He will narrate the story to his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他将为他的小妹妹讲述这个故事。
words.en: If you narrate a story, you tell it from your own point of view.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.ex: The weather today is nasty and rainy.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不愉快，又阴又雨。
words.en: If you describe something as nasty, you mean it is very unpleasant, unattractive, or unkind.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.ex: The smell of rotten food nauseates me.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味让我想吐。
words.en: If something nauseates you, it makes you feel as if you are going to vomit.

words.tr: n. 反对者；否定者；爱唱反调的人
words.ex: Despite the naysayers, she managed to achieve her goals.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有那些摇头族，她还是设法实现了自己的目标。
words.en: A naysayer is someone who always says something will not work or is not possible.

words.tr: adj. 云雾状的；朦胧的；模糊的
words.ex: The nebulous cloud floated slowly across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 那团云雾状的云缓缓飘过天空。
words.en: If you describe something as nebulous, you mean that it is vague and not clearly defined or not easy to describe.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: His dishonesty became his nemesis.
words.ex_cn: 他的不诚实成了他的天谴。
words.en: Someone's nemesis is a person or thing that is very difficult for them to defeat.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: His nickname is 'Speedy' because he runs fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的绰号是‘飞毛腿’，因为他跑得快。
words.en: A nickname is an informal name for someone or something, especially a name that you are called by your friends or family, usually based on your real name or your character.

words.ex: He believes in nihilism and thinks nothing matters.
words.ex_cn: 他相信虚无主义，认为什么都不重要。
words.en: Nihilism is the belief that all values are baseless and that nothing can be known or communicated.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人不愉快的
words.ex: The noisome smell made everyone leave the room.
words.ex_cn: 那股难闻的气味让所有人都离开了房间。
words.en: If you describe something as noisome, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, especially because it has a very strong or bad smell.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.tr: n. 无足轻重的人；不存在
words.ex: He felt like a nonentity in the big meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在大型会议上觉得自己毫无存在感。
words.en: A nonentity is someone who is not important or significant at all.

words.ex: He is a non-partisan judge who treats everyone fairly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位不偏不倚的法官，公平对待每个人。
words.en: Not biased or partisan, especially towards any particular political group.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr: v. 使正常化；使标准化
words.ex: The teacher will normalize the scores to make them fair.
words.ex_cn: 老师会将分数标准化，以使它们更公平。
words.en: To normalize something means to make it normal or to return it to a normal state or condition.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.tr:
n. （长篇）小说；
adj. 新颖的；新奇的；
words.ex: He wrote a novel about a brave girl.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于一个勇敢女孩的小说。
words.en: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.tr:
v. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
n. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
words.ex: He gave me a nudge to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻推了我一下，让我开始这个项目。
words.en: If you nudge someone, you push them gently, usually with your elbow, in order to draw their attention to something.

words.ex: The loud noise every night is a nuisance.
words.ex_cn: 每晚的噪音真是个讨厌的事。
words.en: A nuisance is a person, thing, or situation that is annoying or causes trouble.

words.tr: v. 使无效；抵消；废除；取消
words.ex: The judge will nullify the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法官将宣布该合同无效。
words.en: To nullify something means to make it have no effect or value.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.ex: The obedient child cleaned his room without being told.
words.ex_cn: 这个听话的孩子没被要求就打扫了房间。
words.en: An obedient person or animal does what they are told to do.

words.ex: Children must obey their parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子必须遵守父母的规定。
words.en: To obey means to do what you are told or expected to do according to a rule, law, or someone with authority over you.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.tr: v. 使负义务；使有责任；强制
words.ex: The law obligate him to pay taxes.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使他缴税。
words.en: To obligate someone means to make it necessary for them to do something, especially because of a law, rule, or agreement.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.ex: The loud music was obnoxious and made everyone leave.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐非常讨厌，让所有人都离开了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as obnoxious, you think that they are very unpleasant because of being aggressive, loud, or offensive.

words.ex: The obscene behavior shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这种可憎的行为让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: If you describe something as obscene, you mean it offends you because it relates to sex or violence in a way that you think is unpleasant and shocking.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: His obstinacy in refusing treatment led to his condition worsening.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝治疗的固执态度导致他的病情恶化。
words.en: The quality or state of being obstinate; stubbornness.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: The tooth has an occlusion problem.
words.ex_cn: 这颗牙齿有咬合问题。
words.en: An occlusion is a blockage or closure of a passage or vessel in the body.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.ex: He adds sodium to his food for taste.
words.ex_cn: 他为了味道在食物里加钠。
words.en: Sodium is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal. Sodium is an alkali metal, being in group 1 of the periodic table, because it has a single electron in its outer shell that it readily donates, creating a positively charged ion—the Na⁺ cation.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；非传统的；不落俗套的
words.ex: He likes offbeat movies that no one else understands.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢那些别人都不理解的古怪电影。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as offbeat, you mean that they are different from what is usual or expected in an unusual and appealing way.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.ex: His rude words were an offense to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话冒犯了所有人。
words.en: An offense is a crime or a violation of the law; it can also refer to a feeling of being upset or annoyed by something perceived as insulting or disrespectful.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.tr:
n. 官员；高级职员；
adj. 官方的；正式的；
words.ex: The official announced new rules for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员宣布了节日的新规定。
words.en: An official is a person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization, or something that is authorized or formally recognized.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: The glass has opacity so we cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃不透明，所以我们看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: Opacity refers to the quality of being difficult to see through or understand, often due to a lack of transparency or clarity.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: He opined that the new policy would benefit the company.
words.ex_cn: 他认为新政策将对公司有利。
words.en: To opine means to express an opinion.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.tr: n. 机会主义；投机主义
words.ex: He showed opportunism by taking advantage of the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 他利用危机谋取私利，表现出机会主义。
words.en: Opportunism is the practice of taking advantage of opportunities as and when they arise, regardless of planning or principle.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: The palace showed opulence with golden walls and silk curtains.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿以金墙和丝绸窗帘展现了富裕。
words.en: Opulence is great wealth or luxuriousness.

words.ex: She will organize a meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 她明天将安排一次会议。
words.en: To organize something means to arrange it in a systematic way, especially on a large scale.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: The tree has many colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树上有许多彩色的装饰品。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to make something look more attractive but is usually considered to have no practical purpose.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.ex: The old rules have ossified over time.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧规则随着时间的推移变得僵化了。
words.en: To ossify means to change or develop into bone, or to become fixed and unable to change or develop.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr: adj. 炫耀的；浮华的；卖弄的
words.ex: He wore an ostentatious gold watch to show off his wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一块华丽的金表来炫耀他的财富。
words.en: If you describe something as ostentatious, you disapprove of it because it is expensive and is intended to impress people.

words.ex: They ostracize him for being different.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他与众不同而排斥他。
words.en: To ostracize someone means to exclude them from a society or group.

words.ex: He had an outburst when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时大发雷霆。
words.en: An outburst is a sudden release of strong emotion, often in a way that is unexpected or uncontrolled.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.tr: adj. 夸张的； v. “overblow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The news report was overblown and not true.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻报道太过夸张，不真实。
words.en: If you describe something as overblown, you mean that it is given more importance or is more elaborate than necessary.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.ex: The bus was overcrowd with passengers.
words.ex_cn: 这辆公交车挤满了乘客。
words.en: To fill a space with more people or things than is comfortable or safe.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.tr: v. 制服；压倒；令人折服；使难以忍受
words.ex: The police officer overpowered the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察制服了小偷。
words.en: If you overpower someone, you defeat them because you are stronger than they are.

words.ex: Don't overrate his skills; he is not that good.
words.ex_cn: 不要高估他的能力；他没那么好。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is overrated, you mean that people consider them to be better or more important than they really are.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The judge will overrule the objection.
words.ex_cn: 法官将驳回这个异议。
words.en: If someone in authority overrules a decision or order, they officially decide that it is wrong and change it.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.tr:
n. 和平主义者；反战主义者
adj. 非战主义的
words.ex: He is a pacifist and refuses to fight in wars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名和平主义者，拒绝参与战争。
words.en: A pacifist is someone who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and that disputes should be settled by peaceful means.

words.ex: He tried to pacify the crying baby with a toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个玩具让哭闹的婴儿安静下来。
words.en: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you make them calm or content.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to palliate the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: To palliate means to make something less severe or intense without actually solving the cause of it. It can refer to the easing of physical pain or the attempt to make a fault or crime seem less serious.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；暗淡的；无生气的
words.ex: Her face was pallid after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 久病之后，她的脸色变得苍白。
words.en: If you describe something such as a performance or a piece of writing as pallid, you mean that it is weak and not at all exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.ex: The show pandered to children's tastes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节目迎合了孩子们的口味。
words.en: If you pander to someone or to their wishes, you do everything that they want, often to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.ex: Each participant must sign the form.
words.ex_cn: 每个参与者都必须签署表格。
words.en: A participant is someone who takes part in an activity or event.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.ex: He has a passion for painting.
words.ex_cn: 他对绘画充满激情。
words.en: A very strong feeling of love, hate, anger, enthusiasm, etc.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.ex: Reading books is his favorite pastime.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: A pastime is something that you do because you enjoy it or are interested in it, rather than as a job.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.ex: The cows graze in the pasture.
words.ex_cn: 牛在牧场上吃草。
words.en: Pasture is land covered with grass where animals such as cows and sheep can graze.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.tr: n. 怜悯；悲情；哀婉；凄楚
words.ex: The movie filled us with pathos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让我们充满感动。
words.en: Pathos is a quality in a work of art or literature that evokes feelings of pity or sadness.

words.ex: He is a true patriot who loves his country.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正热爱祖国的爱国者。
words.en: A patriot is someone who loves their country and is willing to defend it against enemies or detractors.

words.tr: n. 赞助人；资助人；老主顾
words.ex: The patron gave money to support the art exhibition.
words.ex_cn: 赞助人捐钱支持了这场艺术展览。
words.en: A patron is a person who supports with money, gifts, efforts, or endorsement an artist, musician, writer, form of art, or charitable cause.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The bill is payable next week.
words.ex_cn: 这笔账单下周应付。
words.en: If an amount of money is payable, it has to be paid or it can be paid.

words.ex: He committed a peccadillo by arriving a few minutes late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到几分钟而犯了一个小错误。
words.en: A peccadillo is a small, unimportant fault or sin.

words.ex: He lost his pecuniary support after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了经济支持。
words.en: Pecuniary means relating to money, especially in terms of financial gain or loss.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.tr:
n. 气恼；讨厌的对象
v. （使）气恼
words.ex: It always peeves me when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当人们迟到时，我总是很恼火。
words.en: If something peeves you, it annoys you.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.tr:
n. （赎罪的）苦行；苦修；忏悔
v. 使...以苦行赎罪
words.ex: He performed penance for his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的罪行忏悔。
words.en: Penance is the act of doing something to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done, especially in some religions.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr: adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: The light is pendent from the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 灯悬挂在天花板上。
words.en: A pendent object is one that hangs down from something else, or a situation that is not yet decided or settled.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: He is penurious and never tips the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他很吝啬，从不给服务员小费。
words.en: If you describe someone as penurious, you mean that they are extremely poor or extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.ex: The percentage of students who passed the test was 85.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生百分比是85。
words.en: A percentage is a proportion or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.ex: Children develop perceptual skills by playing with toys.
words.ex_cn: 儿童通过玩玩具发展知觉能力。
words.en: Relating to the ability to interpret or become aware of something through the senses.

words.tr: adj. 断然的；不容置辩的；专横的
words.ex: He gave a peremptory order to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他下达了一个不容置疑的离开命令。
words.en: If someone's manner or behavior is peremptory, they are so confident and sure of their authority that they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: His perfidy shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的背信弃义让所有人震惊。
words.en: Perfidy is the act of deliberately betraying someone's trust; treachery.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.ex: The climb was perilous in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 在暴风雨中，这次攀登非常危险。
words.en: Full of danger or risk.

words.ex: The moon has a periodic cycle of phases.
words.ex_cn: 月亮的相位变化是周期性的。
words.en: Happening or appearing at regular intervals.

words.tr: adj. 巡游的；到处走的；兼职的
words.ex: He is a peripatetic teacher who moves from town to town.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位四处奔波的老师，从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
