words.en: If you have a peripatetic job or way of life, you travel around a lot, living or working in different places for short periods of time.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.ex: He will perjure himself in court.
words.ex_cn: 他将在法庭上作伪证。
words.en: If someone perjures themselves in a court of law, they lie, even though they have promised to tell the truth.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: He asked for permission to leave early.
words.ex_cn: 他请求允许早点离开。
words.en: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr:
adj. 垂直的；笔直的
n. 垂直线
words.ex: The lines are perpendicular to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些线互相垂直。
words.en: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line; vertical.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: The rain persisted all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨持续了一整天。
words.en: If you persist in doing something, you continue to do it even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: This is my personal notebook.
words.ex_cn: 这是我的个人笔记本。
words.en: Relating to or belonging to a particular person rather than to a group or an organization.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.tr: adj. 颖悟的；敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perspicacious and notices small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 她很敏锐，能注意到细小的错误。
words.en: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things.

words.ex: His speech was persuasive and made everyone agree.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲很有说服力，让所有人都同意了。
words.en: A persuasive argument or reason is one that makes you believe that something is true or right.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: His pessimism made him expect the worst.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲观主义让他总是预期最坏的结果。
words.en: Pessimism is the belief that bad things are going to happen or that something is going to turn out badly.

words.tr: v. 不断打扰；纠缠；烦扰
words.ex: The child keeps pestering his mom for candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子不停地缠着妈妈要糖果。
words.en: If you say that someone is pestering you, you mean that they keep asking you to do something, or keep talking to you, and you find this annoying.

words.ex: The village was destroyed by pestilence last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄被瘟疫摧毁了。
words.en: A pestilence is a fatal epidemic disease, especially bubonic plague.

words.ex: The students handed in a petition to the principal.
words.ex_cn: 学生们向校长递交了一份请愿书。
words.en: A petition is a document signed by a lot of people which asks a government or other official group to do a particular thing.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: He has a phobia of spiders.
words.ex_cn: 他有对蜘蛛的恐怖病。
words.en: A phobia is an extreme or irrational fear of or aversion to something.

words.tr: adj. （非正式）不值钱的；眼光狭小的；微不足道的; n. 价值低微的小硬币；西班牙小币；（非正式...
words.ex: He dismissed her concerns as picayune.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑一顾地认为她的担忧微不足道。
words.en: If you describe something as picayune, you mean that it is very small, unimportant, or trivial.

words.ex: The pied butterfly fluttered among the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 那只杂色蝴蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞。
words.en: Having patches of two or more colors, typically black and white.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.tr: v. 小偷小摸；偷窃（小东西）
words.ex: He was caught pilfering from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他因在商店里小偷小摸被抓。
words.en: To pilfer means to steal things of little value or in small quantities, often in a stealthy way.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；辛辣的；刺激的；迷人的；兴奋的
words.ex: The sauce has a piquant flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种酱汁味道辛辣可口。
words.en: Something that is piquant is pleasantly strong and sharp in taste or smell.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.tr: n. 海盗行为；侵犯版权；
words.ex: The ship was attacked because of piracy near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 船在海岸附近因海盗行为遭到袭击。
words.en: The act of illegally copying and selling someone else's work, especially books, videos, or computer programs, or the act of attacking and stealing from ships at sea.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.tr: adj. 令人怜悯的；使人同情的；可怜的
words.ex: The dog looked pitiful in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe something as pitiful, you mean that it is inadequate or disappointing.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.ex: The violin played a plaintive melody.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴演奏了一首哀伤的旋律。
words.en: A plaintive sound or voice expresses sadness.

words.tr:
n. 塑料；
adj. 塑料的；
words.ex: The bottle is made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是塑料做的。
words.en: A plastic is a material which is produced from oil by a chemical process and which is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: The actor received a plaudit for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而获得赞誉。
words.en: Plaudit refers to an expression of praise or approval, often given in the form of applause or enthusiastic commendation.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: He made a plea for help.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求帮助。
words.en: A plea is a request or an appeal made in an urgent or emotional manner, or a statement made by someone in a court of law in which they say whether they are guilty of a crime or not.

words.tr: v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由
words.ex: He pleaded for help when he was lost.
words.ex_cn: 当他迷路时，他恳求帮助。
words.en: If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.

words.ex: He made a pledge to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了帮助穷人的保证。
words.en: A pledge is a serious promise or agreement, especially one made publicly or officially. It can also refer to something given as security for the fulfillment of a contract or the payment of a debt.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The willow branch is pliant and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 柳枝柔软，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliant person or thing is easily influenced or controlled by others.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.ex: The poignancy of the moment was not lost on anyone.
words.ex_cn: 那一刻的辛酸没有被任何人忽略。
words.en: The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

words.ex: The argument was pointless.
words.ex_cn: 这个争论毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe something as pointless, you are emphasizing that it has no purpose or is not worth doing.

words.ex: The polar bear lives in the Arctic.
words.ex_cn: 北极熊生活在北极。
words.en: relating to the North or South Pole or to the region around it; having opposite extremes or characteristics.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.tr:
n. 光泽；上光剂；
v. 擦亮；润色；
words.ex: The polish of the wooden table made it shine.
words.ex_cn: 木桌的光泽让它闪闪发亮。
words.en: If you polish something, you make it smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance. Polish is also a substance that you use to make things smooth and shiny.

words.tr: adj. 有智虑的；精明的；有策略的
words.ex: It was politic to stay silent during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 在会议上保持沉默是明智的。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as politic, you mean that it is sensible and likely to achieve what you want.

words.ex: The factory releases a pollutant into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向河里排放一种污染物。
words.en: A pollutant is a substance that pollutes something, especially air, water, or soil.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr: adv. 糟糕地；拙劣地；不足；
words.ex: He performed poorly in the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中表现得很糟糕。
words.en: In a manner that is not good or satisfactory.

words.tr: adj. 流行的；受欢迎的；大众的；
words.ex: This song is popular among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中很流行。
words.en: liked, admired, or enjoyed by many people or by a particular person or group

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: This portable charger works well on trips.
words.ex_cn: 这个便携式充电器在旅行时很好用。
words.en: Capable of being carried or moved about with ease.

words.ex: He painted a portrait of his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅他母亲的肖像。
words.en: A portrait is a painting, drawing, or photograph of a particular person.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr: n. 装模作样的人；装腔作势的人
words.ex: He was always seen as a poseur, trying too hard to fit in with the cool crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他总是被视为一个装模作样的人，过于努力地想融入酷酷的群体。
words.en: A poseur is someone who behaves in an artificial way in order to impress other people.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.ex: They decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定把会议推迟到下周。
words.en: To postpone something means to arrange for it to take place at a later time than was originally planned.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: The potency of the medicine helped him recover quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效力帮助他迅速康复。
words.en: Potency refers to the strength, effectiveness, or capacity of something, especially a drug or chemical.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: The potentate ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者以铁腕统治。
words.en: A potentate is a ruler who has great power, especially one who rules over a large area or empire.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.ex: His hard work received much praise from the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力工作得到了老师的许多赞美。
words.en: If you praise someone or something, you express approval for their achievements or qualities.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.ex: This necklace is precious to her.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链对她来说很珍贵。
words.en: If you say that something such as a resource is precious, you mean that it is valuable and should not be wasted or used badly.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the precipice, afraid to move.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边，不敢动。
words.en: A very steep or overhanging place on a cliff or mountain; a situation of great peril.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: n. 事先形成的看法；先入之见；成见
words.ex: He had a preconception that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: An idea or opinion that is formed before you have enough information or experience, or a bias that prevents objective consideration of an issue.

words.tr:
n. 前提；先决条件
v. 预先处理；事先准备
words.ex: You must finish homework as a precondition to play games.
words.ex_cn: 你必须完成作业才能玩游戏。
words.en: A precondition is something that must happen or exist before something else can happen.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.ex: He predetermines the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就决定了结果。
words.en: To decide or settle (something) in advance.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: The old woman predict rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言明天会下雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.ex: His preeminence in the field of medicine is undisputed.
words.ex_cn: 他在医学领域的卓越地位是毋庸置疑的。
words.en: The state of being superior to all others in status, quality, or importance.

words.ex: She is pregnant and will have a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她怀孕了，下个月就要生宝宝了。
words.en: Having a baby developing in the uterus.

words.tr: vt. 预先判断；对……预先作出判决; vi. 预先判断；对未经详察而预作判断
words.ex: It's important not to prejudge the situation before hearing all the facts.
words.ex_cn: 在听到所有事实之前，不预先判断情况是很重要的。
words.en: If you prejudge a situation, you form an opinion about it before you have all the facts.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.ex: He did not premeditate the crime; it happened in the moment.
words.ex_cn: 他没有预谋犯罪；那是当场发生的。
words.en: If you premeditate an action, especially a crime, you plan it or think about it before you do it.

words.ex: She had a premonition that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A premonition is a feeling that something, especially something unpleasant, is going to happen.

words.tr: v. 先占；使全神贯注；占据…的思想
words.ex: The old man preoccupies the best seat in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人先占了公园里最好的座位。
words.en: If something is preoccupying you, you are thinking about it a lot or it is occupying your attention.

words.ex: The preponderance of evidence shows he is guilty.
words.ex_cn: 大多数证据表明他有罪。
words.en: If there is a preponderance of one type of thing or person in a group, there are more of that type than of any other.

words.tr:
adj. 给人良好印象的；令人喜爱的；吸引人的
v. 使预先具有（某种思想）；使…先怀偏见；使产生偏爱；“prepossess”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a prepossessing smile that could light up a room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能照亮整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as prepossessing, you mean that they have a quality that makes you like or approve of them immediately.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: It is the president's prerogative to make final decisions.
words.ex_cn: 做最终决定是总统的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.tr: adj. 规定的；指定的；约定俗成的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prescriptive rule for writing essays.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个关于写论文的规定性规则。
words.en: If something is prescriptive, it involves making rules or giving instructions about what should be done.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.ex: He is presumably at home now.
words.ex_cn: 推测起来，他现在在家。
words.en: If you say that something is presumably the case, you mean that you think it is very likely to be the case, although you are not certain.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.tr: adj. 放肆的；冒昧的；自以为是的
words.ex: He was presumptuous to ask for a raise after just one week.
words.ex_cn: 他才工作一周就要求加薪，太自以为是了。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as presumptuous, you disapprove of them because they are doing something that they have no right or authority to do.

words.tr: v. 预先假定；预料；以…为先决条件
words.ex: He presupposes that everyone likes coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他假设每个人都喜欢咖啡。
words.en: If one thing presupposes another, the first thing cannot be true or exist unless the second thing is true or exists.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔可以防止头部受伤。
words.en: To prevent something means to stop it from happening or to stop someone from doing something.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: He primarily works as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他主要是一名老师。
words.en: You use primarily to say what is mainly true in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: He always follows the principle of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循诚实的原则。
words.en: A principle is a basic idea or rule that explains or controls how something happens or works.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: The family endured years of privation during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭在战争期间经历了多年的贫困。
words.en: Privation is a situation in which you do not have the things that are essential for a comfortable life, such as enough food, clothing, or shelter.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.ex: He has great proficiency in English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: If you show proficiency in something, you show ability or skill at it.

words.tr:
v. 牟取暴利
n. 获暴利的人；投机商
words.ex: The company was accused of profiteering during the pandemic.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司被指控在疫情期间牟取暴利。
words.en: A profiteer is someone who makes large profits in a way that people consider unfair or dishonest, especially by selling goods that are difficult to get at a very high price.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.ex: The profundity of his insights left the audience speechless.
words.ex_cn: 他见解的深刻让观众无言以对。
words.en: Profundity refers to the quality of being profound, which means having deep insight or understanding, or being very intense or extreme.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.ex: The ancient hunter is the progenitor of our family.
words.ex_cn: 这位古代猎人是我们家族的祖先。
words.en: A progenitor is a direct ancestor of someone or the originator of a particular idea or movement.

words.tr: n. 预断病情；预后；预测
words.ex: The prognosis for patients with this disease is generally poor.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的患者预后通常不佳。
words.en: A prognosis is an estimate of the future course and outcome of a disease, especially of the chances of recovery.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr: n. 推进剂；发射药；火箭燃料
words.ex: The rocket uses a strong propellant to fly.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用一种强大的推进剂来飞行。
words.en: A propellant is a substance that is used to move something forward, especially a rocket or a bullet, by creating a force that pushes it.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.ex: He always follows social propriety.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵守社交礼仪。
words.en: Propriety is the quality of being proper, suitable, or appropriate in behavior or conduct.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.ex: His rude comment was a provocation to start a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论是一种挑衅，想引发争斗。
words.en: If you describe someone's action as a provocation, you mean that it is likely to cause a reaction or argument, especially a violent or angry one.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: She showed great prudence in managing her finances.
words.ex_cn: 她在理财方面表现出了极大的谨慎。
words.en: Prudence is the quality of being careful and avoiding risks.

words.tr: adj. 过分拘谨的；装正经的
words.ex: She is prudish about wearing shorts in public.
words.ex_cn: 她对在公共场合穿短裤感到拘谨。
words.en: If you describe someone as prudish, you mean that they are too easily shocked by things relating to sex.

words.ex: The child's psyche was affected by the loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的心灵受到了嘈杂声音的影响。
words.en: The human soul, mind, or spirit.

words.tr: adj. 精神的；灵魂的；心理的；通灵的；
words.ex: He has a psychic connection with his twin brother.
words.ex_cn: 他和双胞胎兄弟有精神上的联系。
words.en: Relating to or denoting faculties or phenomena that are apparently inexplicable by natural laws, especially involving telepathy or clairvoyance.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.ex: Her pulchritude was the talk of the town.
words.ex_cn: 她的美貌是全镇的话题。
words.en: Physical beauty, especially of a woman.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.ex: He is always punctual for class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课总是准时。
words.en: If you are punctual, you do something or arrive somewhere at the right time and are not late.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: The boy got punishment for breaking the window.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为打碎了窗户而受到了处罚。
words.en: Punishment is the act of punishing someone or the state of being punished.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.tr: n. 办伙食者；提供者；供应商；承办商
words.ex: The purveyor brings food to the school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 办伙食者每天早上给学校送饭。
words.en: A purveyor is a person or company that supplies or provides something, especially food or information.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.ex: The putrid meat smelled awful.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的肉闻起来很臭。
words.en: Something that is putrid has decayed and smells very unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 嘎嘎叫声；庸医；冒充内行的人
v. 嘎嘎地叫；大声闲谈；冒充内行
words.ex: The duck made a loud quack.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子发出了响亮的嘎嘎叫声。
words.en: A quack is someone who pretends to have medical skills that they do not really possess. It can also refer to the sound a duck makes.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.ex: He got a teaching qualification last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了教师资格。
words.en: A qualification is a skill or type of experience that you need in order to do a particular job or activity.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: The study focuses on qualitative data, like people's feelings.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究关注定性数据，比如人们的感受。
words.en: relating to, measuring, or measured by the quality of something rather than its quantity.

words.tr: n. 恶心；晕眩；疑虑；不安
words.ex: The smell of the food gave her a qualm.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A qualm is a feeling of uneasiness about whether what you are doing is right.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.ex: We need to quantify the results of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要量化实验的结果。
words.en: If you try to quantify something, you try to calculate how much of it there is.

words.ex: The study uses quantitative data to measure results.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用定量数据来测量结果。
words.en: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.

words.tr:
v. 争吵；吵架；
n. 争吵；口角；
words.ex: They quarrel over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: A quarrel is an angry argument or disagreement between people.

words.tr: adj. 爱争吵的；好争论的
words.ex: He was a quarrelsome man who always started arguments.
words.ex_cn: 他是个爱争吵的人，总是挑起争论。
words.en: If you describe someone as quarrelsome, you mean that they are bad-tempered and often become involved in arguments.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；难以解释的
words.ex: He is queer and proud of who he is.
words.ex_cn: 他是同性恋，并为自己是谁而自豪。
words.en: Queer is used to describe something that is strange or unusual, or someone who is homosexual.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.tr:
n. 遁词；狡辩；支吾以对；争论的小问题
v. 使用遁词；含糊其辞；吹毛求疵
words.ex: His excuse was just a quibble to avoid blame.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口只是逃避责任的遁词。
words.en: To argue or raise objections about a trivial matter or minor detail.

words.tr: v. 加速；使更活跃；刺激
words.ex: The train will quicken as it leaves the station.
words.ex_cn: 火车离开车站时会加快速度。
words.en: To make or become faster or more active.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.tr: adj. 患狂犬病的；狂暴的；疯狂的
words.ex: The rabid dog ran wildly through the street.
words.ex_cn: 那只狂犬在街上狂奔。
words.en: If you describe someone as rabid, you mean that they have very strong and unreasonable opinions or beliefs about a subject, especially in politics.

words.ex: He faced racial discrimination at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中遭遇了种族歧视。
words.en: Relating to the common characteristics of different races of people, especially in the context of social or cultural differences.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: He wore a ragged coat in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿着一件破旧的外套。
words.en: Clothes that are ragged are old and torn.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr: adj. 狂乱无秩序的；喧闹的；难控制的
words.ex: The rambunctious children were causing chaos in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的孩子们在教室里制造混乱。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a child, as rambunctious, you mean that they are full of energy and difficult to control.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.ex: He still feels rancor toward his old boss.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然对他的前老板怀有怨恨。
words.en: A feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.tr: n. 排名；名次； v. “rank”的现在分词；
words.ex: His ranking in the competition is first.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的排名是第一。
words.en: A ranking is a relationship between a set of items such that, for any two items, the first is either 'ranked higher than', 'ranked lower than' or 'ranked equal to' the second.

words.ex: The kidnappers asked for a ransom of $1 million.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪要求一百万美元的赎金。
words.en: A ransom is the money that is demanded for the release of a person who has been kidnapped.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: The car moved at a rapid speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车以迅速的速度行驶。
words.en: A rapid change or event happens very quickly.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: Rare birds can be seen in this forest.
words.ex_cn: 这种森林里可以看到稀有的鸟类。
words.en: Something that is rare is not common and is therefore interesting or valuable.

words.ex: The little rascal stole my cookie.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的孩子偷了我的饼干。
words.en: A rascal is a person who behaves badly or dishonestly but who is usually likable.

words.tr: n. 大量同时出现的事件；
words.ex: There was a rash of burglaries last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月发生了一连串的盗窃案。
words.en: If someone is rash or does rash things, they act without thinking carefully first, and therefore make mistakes or behave foolishly.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr:
v. 毁坏；破坏；劫掠
n. 破坏；蹂躏
words.ex: The storm ravaged the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个小村庄。
words.en: To ravage means to cause severe and extensive damage to something.

words.tr:
n. 渡鸦；乌黑；黑亮
adj. 乌黑的
v. 掠夺；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: A raven flew over the old house.
words.ex_cn: 一只乌鸦飞过了那栋老房子。
words.en: A raven is a large bird of the crow family, with glossy black plumage and a hoarse voice. It is often associated with omens or bad luck. As a verb, it means to seize or devour greedily.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.ex: He will realign his goals after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议后将重新调整他的目标。
words.en: To change the way something is organized or arranged in order to make it more effective or suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The movie shows realism by depicting everyday life honestly.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影通过真实地描绘日常生活展现现实主义。
words.en: Realism is the quality or fact of representing a person, thing, or situation accurately or in a way that is true to life.

words.tr: v. 重新排列；重新安排
words.ex: He rearranged the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他把书架上的书重新排列了。
words.en: If you rearrange the objects in a place, you change the way in which they are organized or positioned.

words.ex: He gave a reasonable answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个合理的回答。
words.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive or extreme.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；退款
v. 减少
words.ex: He got a rebate on his new TV.
words.ex_cn: 他买新电视时得到了一笔回扣。
words.en: A rebate is a partial refund to someone who has paid too much for tax, rent, or a utility.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.tr: v. 重铸；改写；更换（演员）
words.ex: The director decided to recast the play with a different set of actors.
words.ex_cn: 导演决定用另一组演员重新排演这出戏。
words.en: To recast something means to change it by organizing it in a different way or presenting it in a different form.

words.tr: v. 后退；减弱；退出（某种活动）
words.ex: The flood waters begin to recede.
words.ex_cn: 洪水开始退去。
words.en: If something recedes, it becomes more distant or less noticeable.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.tr:
n. 休息；休会；壁龛；壁凹
v. 放入壁龛；休息；休会
words.ex: The children play outside during recess.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在课间休息时到外面玩耍。
words.en: A recess is a break between the periods of work of an official body such as a committee, a court of law, or a government.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.ex: The child gave a recital of poems at school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在学校进行了诗歌朗诵。
words.en: A recital is a performance of music or poetry, usually given by a soloist or a small group.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的；
words.ex: He drove reckless and got into an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他开车鲁莽，结果出了事故。
words.en: If you say that someone is reckless, you mean that they act in a way which shows that they do not care about danger or the effect their behaviour will have on other people.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.ex: He recoiled when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，他退缩了。
words.en: If something makes you recoil, you move your body quickly away from it because it frightens, offends, or hurts you.

words.ex: I can't recollect where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我想不起来把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you recollect something, you remember it.

words.tr: vi. 重新开始; vt. 重新开始
words.ex: After a brief pause, the orchestra recommenced playing.
words.ex_cn: 短暂的停顿后，管弦乐队重新开始演奏。
words.en: To start something again after it has stopped.

words.ex: I recommend this book to you.
words.ex_cn: 我向你推荐这本书。
words.en: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find them good or useful.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: The soldier did reconnaissance before the mission.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在任务前进行了侦察。
words.en: Reconnaissance is the military activity of obtaining information about an enemy's position, strength, or intentions by sending out small groups of soldiers or by using aircraft.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.tr: v. 恢复；重新获得；复原；
words.ex: He will recover from the illness soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会从疾病中恢复。
words.en: If you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again. If you recover something that has been lost or stolen, you find it or get it back.

words.ex: The movie recreates the battle of Waterloo.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影再现了滑铁卢战役。
words.en: To recreate something means to make it exist or happen again, or to make a copy of something that existed in the past.

words.ex: They shouted recrimination at each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此大声指责。
words.en: Recrimination is the act of accusing someone who has accused you of something.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.tr: adj. 直线运动的；形成直线的；用直线围着的
words.ex: The building has a rectilinear design with sharp, straight lines.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑具有直线设计，线条锐利、笔直。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by straight lines.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 反复出现的；再发生的；
words.ex: He has recurrent headaches every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都反复出现头痛。
words.en: Happening or appearing again or repeatedly.

words.ex: We recycle plastic bottles every week.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周回收塑料瓶。
words.en: To recycle means to process used materials so that they can be used again.

words.tr: v. 弥补；兑换；付清；赎回；履行
words.ex: He worked hard to redeem his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: To redeem something means to get it back by paying a sum of money or by doing something to compensate for a fault or mistake.

words.ex: His apology was redemptive and helped heal their friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他的道歉具有救赎意义，帮助修复了他们的友谊。
words.en: Redemptive actions or processes are intended to save someone from evil, suffering, or failure.

words.ex: The sign helped redirect the traffic away from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志帮助将车流改道，避开事故现场。
words.en: To direct something to a new or different place or purpose.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.tr: vt.& vi. 进一步加强，大大增加 vi. 再加倍，翻两番
words.ex: The team redoubled their efforts to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队加倍努力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To redouble your efforts means to try much harder to achieve something, or to increase your efforts significantly.

words.ex: We need to reduce waste in our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.tr: n. 裁判；介绍人；仲裁者
words.ex: The referee blew the whistle for a foul.
words.ex_cn: 裁判吹哨判罚犯规。
words.en: A referee is an official who watches a game or match closely to ensure that the rules are adhered to and sometimes to arbitrate on matters arising from the play.

words.tr: adj. 精炼的； v. 改进；“refine”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The oil company produced refined gasoline.
words.ex_cn: 这家石油公司生产了精炼的汽油。
words.en: If you say that someone is refined, you mean that they are very polite and have good manners and good taste.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.ex: The government announced a major reform in education.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布了教育方面的重大改革。
words.en: If someone reforms a system, they change or improve it.

words.ex: Light is refracted when it passes through a prism.
words.ex_cn: 当光线通过棱镜时会发生折射。
words.en: To cause (light or sound) to change direction when it enters at an angle a medium of different density.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.tr: v. 使恢复精力；使复原；使变新
words.ex: A short nap can refresh you.
words.ex_cn: 小睡一会儿能让你恢复精力。
words.en: To refresh someone means to make them feel less tired or less hot.

words.ex: The animals found refuge in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物在森林中找到了避难所。
words.en: A place or state of safety or shelter from danger, trouble, or difficulty.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.tr: v. 重新刷新；翻新；整修
words.ex: They will refurbish the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新这栋老房子。
words.en: To refurbish something means to clean it, decorate it, and provide it with new equipment or facilities, especially so that it is more attractive or more useful.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr: adj. 皇家的；尊贵的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: The queen wore a regal crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着一顶威严的王冠。
words.en: If you describe something as regal, you mean that it is suitable for a king or queen, because it is very impressive or beautiful.

words.tr:
v. 看待；有关；
n. 尊敬；致意；
words.ex: I regard him as a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他看作好朋友。
words.en: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

words.ex: Lizards can regenerate their tails.
words.ex_cn: 蜥蜴可以再生尾巴。
words.en: To regenerate means to grow or form again, especially after being damaged or lost, or to improve a place or system by making it more active or successful.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.tr:
v. 倒退；退步；退化
n. 倒退；退步；退化
words.ex: The patient regressed to a childlike state after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，病人退回到了孩童般的状态。
words.en: If you regress, you return to a previous and less advanced stage of development.

words.tr: adv. 定期地；经常地；有规律地；
words.ex: He visits his grandparents regularly.
words.ex_cn: 他定期去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: At consistent intervals or in a consistent manner.

words.ex: The thermostat helps regulate the room temperature.
words.ex_cn: 恒温器有助于调节室温。
words.en: To regulate something means to control or manage it, especially by means of rules or laws.

words.tr: v. 反胃；回吐；依样复述
words.ex: He felt sick and began to regurgitate after eating the spoiled food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了变质的食物后感到恶心，开始反胃。
words.en: To bring up and expel (food) from the stomach to the mouth, as in some birds feeding their young; to repeat (information) without understanding or thought.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr:
n. (旧东西的)改作；旧调重弹的作品
v. （稍微改动）重新推出；炒冷饭；重谈老调
words.ex: The movie is just a rehash of an old story.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影只是对老故事的改作。
words.en: To rehash something means to present it again in a slightly different form, especially in a way that is not very interesting or original.

words.ex: The actors had a rehearsal before the play.
words.ex_cn: 演出前，演员们进行了一次排练。
words.en: A rehearsal of a play, dance, or piece of music is a practice of it in preparation for a performance.

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: They rejoice when the sun comes out.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳出来时，他们欢呼。
words.en: To feel or show great joy or delight.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.tr: n. 再发；重陷；故态复萌；
words.ex: He had a relapse after stopping his medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他停药后病情复发了。
words.en: If someone relapses, they return to a less advanced state, or to a previous way of behaving that they wanted to change.

words.tr: v. 有关；把…联系起来；认同；叙述；理解；
words.ex: This story relates to your childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事与你的童年有关。
words.en: If you relate a story, you tell it. If two things relate, they are connected in some way.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.tr: adj. 信任的；信赖的；依靠的
words.ex: He is reliant on his friend for help.
words.ex_cn: 他信任朋友来帮助他。
words.en: A person or thing that is reliant on someone or something else depends on them for support or help.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.ex: They decided to relocate to a quieter town.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定搬到一个更安静的城镇。
words.en: to move to a new place and establish one's home or business there

words.ex: He showed reluctance to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他表现出不愿意在全班面前讲话。
words.en: Reluctance is an unwillingness to do something.

words.ex: Children rely on their parents for food and shelter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们依靠父母提供食物和住所。
words.en: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可挽救的；可矫正的
words.ex: The damage to the environment is remediable if we act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们迅速采取行动，对环境的破坏是可以补救的。
words.en: If something is remediable, it can be corrected or cured.

words.ex: He took a remedial math course to improve his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一门补救数学课程来提高自己的技能。
words.en: Remedial actions or activities are intended to correct something that is wrong or to improve a bad situation.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He felt a warm reminiscence of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了对童年的温馨回忆。
words.en: The act or process of recalling past experiences, events, etc.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.ex: The committee issued a remonstrance against the proposed changes.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对拟议的变更提出了抗议。
words.en: A remonstrance is a formal statement of protest or complaint.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: The removal of the old tree made the yard bigger.
words.ex_cn: 移除那棵老树让院子变大了。
words.en: The act of removing something or someone from a place or position.

words.ex: He received fair remuneration for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他因工作获得了公平的报酬。
words.en: Remuneration refers to the money that is paid to someone for the work that they have done.
